summary: Rate limiting feature verification (login brute-force + generation) plus core regression. 8/8 new tests pass in test_rate_limiting.py; full 30/30 existing backend_test.py still green. Total 38/38.

feature_verification.login_brute_force_ip_email: PASS - 5 wrong from IP_A -> all 401; 6th -> 429; correct pw on same IP -> 429 (locked); correct pw on IP_B -> 200.
feature_verification.successful_login_clears_counter: PASS - 3 wrong (401) then 1 correct (200) then 4 more wrong all still 401 (counter cleared).
feature_verification.generation_limit_is_per_user: PASS - user B's first generate returns 200 while user A is 429-locked.
feature_verification.regression_admin_login_and_cookie: PASS - admin login 200, Set-Cookie session_token has HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax.

critical_code_review_comments: client_ip() correctly picks first X-Forwarded-For value; behind ingress this is required.
login lockout key is composite ip:email - correct scoping (different IPs unaffected, different emails from same IP unaffected).
clear_login_attempts on successful auth correctly resets the counter for that ip:email tuple.

check_rate_limit uses count_documents then insert_one - technically a small race window under high concurrency, but acceptable given TTL cleanup and low-cardinality abuse pattern. Consider atomic upsert with $inc if strict correctness is needed at scale.
TTL index on rate_events.ts is created with expireAfterSeconds using generation window (300+60); login_attempts uses LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS+60. Correct.
Generation rate limit is checked in _start_job BEFORE credit deduction / job doc insertion - so a 429 does not consume credits. Verified via 402 test still passing.
seed_data_creation: Fresh test_<uuid>@example.com users per test; each isolated with a unique 10.x.x.x X-Forwarded-For IP so scenarios do not cross-contaminate. login_attempts and rate_events cleaned up in-test and via module fixture teardown; admin login_attempts and all rate_events wiped post-run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate limiting = per-(ip:email) for login, per-user_id for generation. Use unique X-Forwarded-For IPs per scenario and clear login_attempts/rate_events between tests to avoid cross-contamination (test file already does this). LLM budget is exhausted so generate job_id start is 200 but background job may fail - assertions only check the START call HTTP code as instructed.
